taskloom Configuration.

These fields map to `~/.taskloom/config.yaml` (and the per-project `.taskloom/config.yaml`). The canonical machine-readable form is the JSON Schema at `resources/schema/input/taskloom-config-schema.json`.

## Overriding From The Environment Or A CLI Flag

Every field on this page can also be set without editing a config file, in ascending precedence: the home config file, then the project config file, then an environment variable, then a `--config-set` flag — the last one that sets a given key wins.

An environment variable override starts with `TASKLOOM_CONFIG_`, followed by the field's dotted path with each segment upper-cased and joined by `_` (e.g. `agents.mycoder.runtime` becomes `TASKLOOM_CONFIG_AGENTS_MYCODER_RUNTIME`). A CLI override uses the repeatable `--config-set <dotted.path>=<value>` flag (`--config-set agents.mycoder.runtime=container-rootless`) — never a per-field flag of its own, since a command's OWN flags (`--format`, `--bundle`, ...) are not config overrides. Both forms are matched case-insensitively against whatever your config file already has, adopting its casing; unlike an environment variable's name, `--config-set`'s path preserves whatever case you type, so it can also CREATE a new case-sensitive key (e.g. `--config-set agents.MyCoder.runtime=container-rootless`), which an environment variable cannot do.

For example, `homing` can be set via `TASKLOOM_CONFIG_HOMING=<value>` or `--config-set homing=<value>`.

## Top-Level Fields

Schema for taskloom's own config.yaml files (~/.taskloom/config.yaml and the per-project .taskloom/config.yaml), layered via internal/shared/confload exactly like ctxloom's own config-schema.json.

| Field | Type | Description |
|-------|------|-------------|
| `homing` | string | Where the project's task-store log is homed. "home" keeps it PRIVATE under ~/.ctxloom/tasks/<project-id>.jsonl (today's default behavior; never committed, never shared by a clone). "repo" checks the log into the project tree at .taskloom/tasks.jsonl, alongside this config file, so it is SHAREABLE and travels with clones. Unset (at every layer: this key, the TASKLOOM_CONFIG_HOMING environment variable, and --homing) resolves silently to "home" — the pre-homing status quo, a no-op for every existing project. Only an explicitly INVALID value (anything other than "home"/"repo") is a returned error naming the bad value and the valid set. Allowed values: `home`, `repo`. |
| `tag_schema` | string[] | Tag-schema declarations, each written in tagma's own tag syntax, asserting a facet over a tag key used on this project's tasks — e.g. `tagma.arity:"triage:kind"=scalar`. Facets: `arity` (a target declared `=scalar` may carry at most one tag with that (namespace, key) per task, and taskloom's write seam collapses a re-tag onto it — the newest value survives; the log still records both the retracting untag and the new tag, so history is never rewritten); `priority_fn`/`decay_fn` (`tagma.priority_fn:"<target>"="<mustache-equation>"`, `tagma.decay_fn:"<target>"="<mustache-equation>"` — mustache-form formulas EVALUATED read-time by internal/shared/tasks/priority.Compute against every task's tag values plus taskloom-provided built-ins like age_days; exactly one of each may be declared across every target, or `taskloom list --sort priority`/`task_list`'s sort="priority" fails loud); `enum` (`tagma.enum:"<target>"="a,b,c"` — a closed value vocabulary `taskloom lint` checks a tag's value against); `range` (`tagma.range:"<target>"="min,max"` — a numeric [min,max] bound `taskloom lint` checks a tag's value against, and implies the value must parse as a number); `hide` (`tagma.hide:"<target>"=<bool>` — display-time-only tag hiding, never enforced at write time or affecting storage/matching/ranking); `type` (`tagma.type:"<target>"=<name>` — tagma's client-loadable type comparison, SPEC.md §9: switches that target's relational-operator matching ('>' '>=' '<' '<=') from tagma's own numeric grammar to a registered comparator. taskloom registers exactly one name, `semver`, for full SemVer 2.0.0 precedence — also enforced at write time, rejecting a value that doesn't parse as one). See internal/shared/tasks/tagschema, internal/shared/tasks/priority, and internal/shared/tasks/lint. This key replaces the WHOLE list at whichever layer sets it last (home < project < TASKLOOM_CONFIG_* env < --config-set) — it is never merged element-by-element. Unset at every layer falls back to taskloom's built-in triage-classification baseline: `triage:level`/`triage:kind`/`triage:effort`/`triage:blocks-release` declared scalar (`triage:level` is the consequence ladder, an integer 1-5 with 1 the worst — see docs/task-tagging-standard.md for what each rung means; `triage:kind` is a work-kind enum — defect/capability/chore; `triage:effort` is a 0-5 range; `triage:blocks-release` is also declared `type=semver`, e.g. `0.7.0`, so a query like `triage:blocks-release<=0.7.0` orders by real version precedence); `triage:exposed` also declares an enum (wire/cli/config/on-disk/api) without being scalar. Priority is DERIVED read-time from `triage:level` — each rung is worth twice the one below it, an untagged task floors BELOW the mildest rung — adjusted by the age curve, doubled when `triage:blocks-release` is present, and divided by `triage:effort`; `triage:kind` drives the decay curve rather than the score. The factual flags (`triage:crashes`, `triage:data-loss`, `triage:no-workaround`, `triage:security=<cwe>`, `triage:regression=<version-or-sha>`) are searchable labels that no formula reads; `triage:exposed`/`triage:blind-gate` are read by decay_fn, and `triage:exploited-in-wild` forces a task's derived priority to the ceiling outright. |
